new.note: The territorial restriction goes beyond the household restriction in Exodus 12:19 and differs from the direction to eat unleavened bread.

new.title: Moses appoints leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens
new.speaker: Moses
new.note: Moses appoints officers as Jethro had advised. The appointment and delegated judgments are reported in verses 25–26.

new.speaker: the Lord through Moses

new.speaker: the psalmist (David)
new.recipient: God, in the hearing of worshippers
new.note: Maxim inside a prayer; related to Proverbs 27:5–6 (AUD-22-27-5).

new.title: A call for all flesh to bless the Lord's holy name
new.speaker: the psalmist (David)
new.note: Jussive call to humanity, not addressed to God; compare Greek Psalm 150 record.

new.title: The ungodly urge one another to revel because life is short
new.speaker: The ungodly, as reported by the wisdom writer
new.note: The author's literary portrait quotes the ungodly urging each other to indulge. The author expressly rejects their reasoning in 2:21–24.

new.title: The ungodly resolve to oppress the poor, widows and the old
new.speaker: The ungodly, as reported by the wisdom writer
new.note: The proposal is spoken by the ungodly in the author's literary portrait. The author expressly rejects their reasoning in 2:21–24.

new.title: The ungodly plot to entrap, torture, and kill the righteous person
new.speaker: The ungodly, as reported by the wisdom writer
new.note: The proposal is spoken by the ungodly in the author's literary portrait. The author expressly rejects their reasoning in 2:21–24.

new.title: Wickedness blinds people to the reward of holiness
new.speaker: The wisdom writer (speaking as Solomon)

new.title: Those who trust God understand truth, and the faithful remain in His love
new.speaker: The wisdom writer (speaking as Solomon)

new.title: Those who despise wisdom and discipline have empty hope
new.speaker: The wisdom writer (speaking as Solomon)

new.title: Blessed are the undefiled barren woman and the faithful eunuch
new.speaker: The wisdom writer (speaking as Solomon)

new.title: Childlessness with virtue is better, for virtue is remembered
new.speaker: The wisdom writer (speaking as Solomon)

new.title: Honorable old age is understanding and a spotless life
new.speaker: The wisdom writer (speaking as Solomon)

new.title: The allure of wickedness obscures good and corrupts innocent minds
new.speaker: The wisdom writer (speaking as Solomon)

new.title: The ungodly discover that pride and riches left them without virtue
new.speaker: The wisdom writer (speaking as Solomon)

new.title: The hope of the ungodly blows away; the righteous live for ever
new.speaker: The wisdom writer (speaking as Solomon)
new.note: 5:17–23 picture God arming creation for judgment; description, not counsel.

new.title: Envy has no share in wisdom, and wise people help preserve the world
new.speaker: The wisdom writer (speaking as Solomon)
new.note: 6:22 announces the teaching; 6:24 grounds the call of 6:25 (ot-wisdom-of-solomon-v6-25).

new.title: Even a king shares the common mortal birth and death
new.speaker: The wisdom writer (speaking as Solomon)

new.title: The sage teaches that God loves the one who dwells with wisdom
new.speaker: The wisdom writer (speaking as Solomon)
new.note: 7:15–26 are prayer, autobiography and praise of wisdom rather than counsel.

new.title: Companionship with wisdom brings gladness and joy
new.speaker: The first-person royal wisdom narrator
new.note: Declarative sayings on wisdom's benefits continuing AUD-26-8-5 (8:5–9); could instead extend it. 8:10–15 are first-person expectations.

new.title: The sage recognizes that wisdom is God’s gift
new.speaker: The first-person royal wisdom narrator
new.note: States a maxim: knowing whose gift wisdom is is itself understanding; leads into the prayer. Cf. James 1:5 (A037).

new.title: Passing wisdom by brings harm; wisdom rescues those who serve her
new.speaker: The wisdom writer
new.note: Lesson drawn from the Sodom example; the rest of chapter 10 retells history and needs no record.

new.title: Devotion to God is stronger than everything
new.speaker: The wisdom writer
new.note: Lesson stated within the Jacob retelling ('so that he might know').

new.title: One is punished by the very things by which one sins
new.speaker: The wisdom writer
new.note: Governing maxim of chs. 11–19, restated at 12:23, 12:27 and 16:1; counterpart principle at 11:5.

new.title: Wretched are those who hope in lifeless, man-made gods
new.speaker: The wisdom writer
new.note: Woe; the woodcarver satire in 13:11–19 illustrates it (cf. Isaiah 44:9–20); link those verses as context.

new.title: The ungodly and their ungodliness are equally hateful to God
new.speaker: The wisdom writer
new.note: 14:8 curses idol and maker; 14:9–10 generalize that the deed is punished together with the doer.

new.title: Idol worship is the beginning, cause and end of every evil
new.speaker: The wisdom writer
new.note: Same maxim at 14:12 (beginning of sexual immorality); vice list 14:22–26 shows its fruit; link as Additional Scripture.

new.title: Justice pursues false oaths, whatever one swears by
new.speaker: The wisdom writer
new.note: Maxim on perjury: punishment comes from justice, not from the gods sworn by; cf. Leviticus 19:12 (C0604).

new.title: Wickedness is cowardly, condemned by its own conscience
new.speaker: The wisdom writer
new.note: General maxims on conscience and fear drawn from the plague of darkness; cf. Proverbs 28:1.

new.title: Israel at the Passover pledges to share blessings and dangers alike
new.speaker: the holy children of Israel
new.recipient: one another, the people of Israel
new.note: Communal pact reported in the Passover retelling ('established the divine law'); not in Exodus 12. Include only if such pledges count.

new.title: The woman is told to follow the flocks to the shepherds' tents
new.speaker: A responding voice in the Song
new.recipient: the woman addressed as beautiful among women
new.note: Direct speech within the poem. The speaker’s identity is not named in this verse.

new.title: A call to catch the little foxes that spoil the vineyards
new.speaker: A voice in the Song
new.recipient: the addressee in the vineyard poem
new.note: Direct speech in the Song’s poetic imagery. The verse does not name its speaker or addressee.

new.title: Honor the Lord and fear no other
new.speaker: The wisdom teacher
new.note: The Greek-lettered verse directly counsels the son to honor the Lord and fear no other. The separate 7:1 record concerns keeping the teacher’s sayings.
new.restored_from: Independent context review of the Saints Translation at Proverbs 7:1a

new.title: The Lord tells Judah to stop bringing futile offerings and festivals
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: the rulers and people of Judah and Jerusalem
new.note: 1:12–13 'you will no longer continue… it is futile' forbids empty worship; 1:15 refuses bloodstained prayers. Covers P01874.

new.title: Isaiah summons the house of Jacob to walk in the Lord's light
new.speaker: Isaiah

new.title: The Lord summons Judah to judge between Him and His vineyard
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: the men of Judah and residents of Jerusalem
new.note: 5:3 (shown as context) has no record; its summons to judge introduces 5:4's question.

new.title: Woe to those who join house to house and field to field
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor

new.title: Woe to those who chase strong drink and ignore the Lord's works
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah

new.title: Woe to those who drag sin along as with a cord
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: 5:19 is a Study Context record; the woes of 5:20–24 are AUD-28-5-20.

new.title: Isaiah calls the house of David to hear and names Emmanuel
new.speaker: Isaiah, delivering the Lord's sign
new.recipient: Ahaz and the house of David
new.note: Naming command, like 'you shall call his name Jesus'. Matthew 1:23 quotes it within AUD-44-1-20.
new.review_note: The summons to hear is in verse 13. The naming of Emmanuel accompanies the sign in verse 14.

new.title: Ephraim and Samaria urge each other to build a tower with hewn stone
new.speaker: the people of Ephraim and Samaria
new.note: Proud 'come, let us' resolve, recorded like the Babel builders' plan (ot-genesis-v11-4).

new.title: Woe to those who write unjust decrees that rob the poor
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah

new.title: Zion's inhabitants are called to exult in Israel's Holy One
new.speaker: Voices in Isaiah's song of thanksgiving
new.note: Call to praise addressed to people; closes the song whose 12:4–5 calls are only a Study Context record (ot-isaiah-v12-4).

new.title: Babylon’s people are told to wail, for the Lord’s day is near
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah (oracle against Babylon)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Prophetic summons to wail, like recorded ot-isaiah-v23-6 and ot-jeremiah-v6-26.

new.title: Moab is called to wail and mourn in sackcloth over its ruin
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah (oracle against Moab)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 15:3 (context verse, outside candidate list) continues the summons: sackcloth, beating, wailing. Isaiah 15 has no records.

new.title: The Lord called Jerusalem to weeping, shaving and sackcloth
new.speaker: the Lord Sabaoth (reported by Isaiah)
new.note: Outside candidate list. Reported summons to mourn; ot-isaiah-v22-13 records the people feasting instead.

new.title: Unnamed gatherers are told to gather Israel’s sons one by one
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Command within the 'on that day' promise; compare recorded ot-isaiah-v43-6 (release My sons and daughters).

new.title: Woe to those who plan in secret and apart from the Lord
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: Ethical woe, like recorded AUD-28-5-20; 30:1 ('a plan not through Me', context-adjacent, unrecorded) makes the same charge.

new.title: Turning back to God brings salvation; trust in futile things fails
new.speaker: the Lord, Israel’s Holy One, through Isaiah
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse). Call to return that was refused, like recorded ot-jeremiah-v6-16.

new.title: Blessed are those who remain in the Lord
new.speaker: Isaiah
new.note: Beatitude ('Blessed are those remaining in Him') after the promise that God waits to show mercy.

new.title: Woe to those trusting horses and chariots rather than the Holy One
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: 30:1–2 (woe to those going down to Egypt without asking God; unrecorded) is the same charge; link as Additional Scripture.

new.title: Whoever walks righteously and refuses bribes will dwell secure
new.speaker: Isaiah
new.note: Outside candidate list. Entrance saying like Greek Psalm 14: upright speech, no bribes, shunning bloodshed and injustice.

new.title: Hezekiah receives a three-year sign for eating and planting
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: Hezekiah and the remnant of Judah
new.topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor
new.note: Parallel 2 Kings 19:29 is also unrecorded; link it as Additional Scripture.

new.title: The Lord appoints His servant to bring judgment to the nations
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: the Lord’s servant (named Jacob/Israel in this text)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 42:1 and 42:4 are outside the candidate list. Matthew 12:18–21 quotes it (inside AUD-44-12-15); the 42:5–9 commission is AUD-28-42-5.

new.title: The deaf and blind are summoned to listen and look
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: Israel, the spiritually deaf and blind
new.note: Call to perceive addressed to the people (42:19 names God’s servants); bare 'hear' summonses are often Study Context.

new.title: God tells Israel to remember and confess its lawless acts first
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: 'You, state your lawless acts first, so that you may be justified': a call to confession in the trial speech.

new.title: The Lord commissions His anointed Cyrus to free His people
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 44:28–45:1 and 45:3–6 are outside the candidate list. Cyrus’s call is also recalled in 41:2, 46:11 and 48:14–15.

new.title: The servant receives a tongue for instruction and an ear to hear
new.speaker: the Lord (reported by the servant)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Third Servant Song: equipped for a speaking task, and obedient ('I do not disobey'); records at 50:8 and 50:10 follow.

new.title: The unjust are tossed like waves; the ungodly have no joy
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: Outside candidate list. 48:22 (context verse) repeats 'There is no rejoicing for the ungodly'; link as Additional Scripture.

new.title: The Lord appoints unceasing watchmen on Jerusalem’s walls
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Appointed guards 'will never be silent as they remember the Lord'; compare ot-isaiah-v21-6.

new.title: The Lord puts His words in Jeremiah’s mouth, setting him over nations
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: 1:9 is a context verse; the mandate is 'to uproot, demolish, destroy, build and plant'.

new.title: Your own evil disciplines you; abandoning the Lord is bitter
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: 'Know and see that abandoning Me is bitter': maxim with a call to recognize it; 2:17 and 4:18 make the same point.

new.title: Israel is called to acknowledge its iniquity against the Lord
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Content of the message Jeremiah is sent to proclaim (ot-jeremiah-v3-12); addressed to Israel, so a separate record.

new.title: Judah is told to wear sackcloth and wail at the Lord’s fury
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Summons to mourn in the alarm oracle of 4:5–8 (ot-jeremiah-v4-5, ot-jeremiah-v4-6); compare ot-jeremiah-v6-26.

new.title: Heralds are told to warn the nations and Jerusalem of invaders
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 'Remind the nations… Announce in Jerusalem': a warning summons like ot-jeremiah-v4-5.

new.title: Jeremiah is given the answer to why the Lord brought disaster
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Scripted reply ('you will say to them'): they served foreign gods, so they will serve foreigners in a foreign land.

new.title: The Lord appoints Jeremiah to test His people’s ways
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Appointment as assayer ('I have made you a tester'); 6:30 is Study Context (ot-jeremiah-v6-30).

new.title: Judah is told to amend its ways so God will settle it
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.recipient: all Judea at the Lord’s house
new.note: Core call of the temple sermon; 7:5–6 (ot-jeremiah-v7-5) spells out the amendment.

new.title: Judah is told to go to Shiloh and see what God did
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Warning by example: what God did to Shiloh because of Israel’s evil.

new.title: Jerusalem is told to cut off her hair and raise a lament
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Prophetic summons to mourn the rejected generation, like the recorded calls at 6:26, 9:17 and 22:10.

new.title: Israel is told to say false gods will perish from the earth
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Scripted answer to idolaters ('This is what you will say to them'); distinct from records 10:1–2 and 10:5.

new.title: Jeremiah is told to deliver the saying of the filled wineskins
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Scripted saying and reply ('you will say to this people… then you will say'), like the recorded reply at 23:33.

new.title: Jeremiah is given the answer: to death, sword, famine and captivity
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Scripted reply to 'Where shall we go out?' Alternatively extend ot-jeremiah-v15-1 (15:1, 'Send this people away').

new.title: God tells Jeremiah how he may stand before Him and speak as His mouth
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: 15:19 (context verse) holds the directive: return, bring out the honored from the unworthy, do not turn to them; echoes 1:18.

new.title: Jeremiah is told how to answer when asked why disaster comes
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Scripted reply: their fathers abandoned God and did not keep His law, and this generation did worse.

new.title: God tells Jeremiah to smash the jar as a sign
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The sign-act itself; 19:1 (get the jar) and 19:11 (Study Context, its meaning) are recorded, the smashing is not.

new.title: The Lord condemns the king for building with injustice and withheld wages
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Ethical woe like Hab 2:6–12 (AUD-39-2-6); 22:15–16 ties judging the poor’s case to knowing God; echoes Lev 19:13 (C0607).

new.title: The Lord orders Jeconiah recorded as an outcast
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Decree on Jeconiah’s line ('Record this man as an outcast'); compare the recorded naming order for Pharaoh Neco (26:17).

new.title: Jeremiah tells Seraiah to sink the scroll as a sign against Babylon
new.speaker: Jeremiah instructing Seraiah to act out the Lord's oracle
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The sign-act itself (bind a stone to the scroll, throw it in); record 28:64 holds only the interpreting words.

new.title: Moab’s shattering is to be announced in Zogora
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 'Announce it in Zogora': a summons like recorded 27:2 (announce Babylon’s capture) and 31:17–19.

new.title: The priests and false prophets demand a death sentence for Jeremiah
new.speaker: the priests and false prophets
new.recipient: Judah’s rulers and all the people
new.note: Formal charge at Jeremiah’s trial (MT 26:11), like the first-pass demand at 45:4–5. Recording it does not approve it.

new.title: Jehoiakim sends men to Egypt, and they bring back Uriah
new.speaker: King Jehoiakim
new.note: Reported order of a wicked king; Uriah is then executed (MT 26:22–23).

new.title: Jeremiah is told to answer Shemaiah and rebuke the priest Zephaniah
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Greek-order text: 'I did not send you' to Shemaiah; Zephaniah reminded of his appointment as overseer to confine raving prophets (36:26).

new.title: Restored Israel is told to plant vineyards in Samaria and praise
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Imperatives in the restoration oracle ('plant and praise'), like the recorded calls at 38:7 and 38:21.

new.title: Zedekiah's covenant requires Jerusalem's slaveholders to free Hebrew slaves
new.speaker: King Zedekiah, by covenant with the people
new.note: Royal covenant of release (MT 34:8–10; also 41:15), distinct from the Torah law God recalls in ot-jeremiah-v41-14.

new.title: The officials summon Baruch to read the scroll to them
new.speaker: the officials (rulers) of Judah
new.recipient: Baruch son of Neriah, through Jehudi
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 'Take… the roll… and come'; 'Read it again to us' (43:15, context); then 'Let us certainly report all these words to the king.'

new.title: Jehoiakim sends Jehudi to fetch the scroll
new.speaker: King Jehoiakim
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported royal order (MT 36:21); the officials’ earlier summons of Baruch (43:14–16) is a first-pass finding.

new.title: Elnathan, Gedaliah and Gemariah urge the king not to burn the scroll
new.speaker: Elnathan, Gedaliah and Gemariah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse); a reported request the king ignored (MT 36:25).

new.title: Jehoiakim orders Baruch and Jeremiah arrested
new.speaker: King Jehoiakim
new.recipient: Jerahmeel the king’s son and Seraiah son of Azriel
new.note: Explicit reported order (MT 36:26); the officials’ warning to hide is ot-jeremiah-v43-19.

new.title: Zedekiah sends envoys asking Jeremiah to pray for them
new.speaker: King Zedekiah, through Jehucal and Zephaniah
new.note: A separate occasion from 21:2 (ot-jeremiah-v21-2): different envoys and a request for intercession.

new.title: Jeremiah begs Zedekiah not to send him back to Jonathan’s house
new.speaker: Jeremiah

new.title: Zedekiah orders Jeremiah held in the prison court with daily bread
new.speaker: King Zedekiah
new.note: Reported royal order in a context verse (not a listed candidate); no record covers 44:21.

new.title: The officials demand Jeremiah's death from Zedekiah
new.speaker: the officials of Judah
new.note: 'Let that man be killed!'; the king answers 'He is in your hands' (45:5). Recording the demand does not approve it.

new.title: Zedekiah orders Ebed-melech to take thirty men and rescue Jeremiah
new.speaker: King Zedekiah
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours

new.title: Ebed-melech tells Jeremiah to put the rags beneath the ropes
new.speaker: Ebed-melech
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
new.note: Uncovered directive two verses after the candidate (not listed): 'Put these beneath the ropes. Jeremiah did so.'

new.title: Ishmael invites the mourning pilgrims to Gedaliah as a ruse
new.speaker: Ishmael son of Nethaniah
new.recipient: eighty pilgrims from Shechem, Salem and Samaria
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Deceitful invitation (‘Come in to Gedaliah’) before the massacre (MT 41:6–7).

new.title: God sends Ezekiel to the rebellious house of Israel
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Ezekiel’s call proper ('stand on your feet… I am sending you… you will say to them'); only 2:6 and 2:8 are recorded.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to announce that the end has come on Israel
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Order to proclaim ('say, Thus says the Lord to the land of Israel'); such orders are Commission records at 6:3 and 11:4.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to look north and see the people’s lawlessness
new.speaker: the Lord (in the vision)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: First order of the temple vision tour, like ot-ezekiel-v8-9; 8:6 adds ‘you will yet see greater lawlessness’.

new.title: The Lord tells Ezekiel to eat and drink in anguish as a sign
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Sign-act; its meaning (12:19) has a Study Context record, the command itself has none.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against Israel’s false prophets
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Commission with the opening woe on those who prophesy from their own heart; 13:8 and 13:11 are Study Context only.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against the women who prophesy falsely
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: 'Set your face firmly against the daughters of your people'; the 13:18 woe is Study Context only.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to testify to Jerusalem about her lawlessness
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: 16:3 has only a Study Context record (ot-ezekiel-v16-3); compare the first-pass extension of ot-ezekiel-v22-3 to 22:2.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to tell Israel the parable of the eagles
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Opening charge; only the explanation (17:11–15, AUD-30-17-11) is recorded; 17:3 has a Study Context record only.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to take up a lament over Israel's ruler
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 19:2 has only a Study Context record; the charge to lament is unrecorded.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to confront the elders with their fathers' lawlessness
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Distinct from the later charge at 20:27 (ot-ezekiel-v20-27).

new.title: God tells the house of Israel to remove their idolatrous practices
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.note: Present call to put away practices; 20:7 (ot-ezekiel-v20-7) only recalls the Exodus generation's command.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against the forest of the Negev
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: 21:3 has only a Study Context record; the commission itself is unrecorded.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to mark out two roads for Babylon's sword
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Symbolic act: a signpost where the road forks toward Rabbah and Jerusalem.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy the sword against the Ammonites
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

new.title: Ezekiel is told to address the land and its violent leaders
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Outside candidate list; the oracle 22:23–31 against leaders, priests and people has no record.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to record the day Babylon besieged Jerusalem
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; distinct from the cauldron-parable charge at 24:3 (ot-ezekiel-v24-3).

new.title: Ezekiel is told not to mourn publicly for his wife's death
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Sign-act wholly unrecorded; 24:16–17 outside candidate list; 24:18 records his obedience; 24:22–24 applies the sign to Israel.

new.title: The exiles ask Ezekiel to explain his refusal to mourn
new.speaker: the people in exile
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse); the request is answered by the oracle recorded at 24:21 (ot-ezekiel-v24-21).

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against the Ammonites
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; 25:3 has only a Study Context record (ot-ezekiel-v25-3).

new.title: Ezekiel is told to confront the ruler of Tyre's claim to divinity
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; the oracle 28:1–10 has no record.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to lament over the ruler of Tyre
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The lament 28:11–19 has no record.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against Sidon
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 28:22 has only a Study Context record (ot-ezekiel-v28-22).

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against Pharaoh and all Egypt
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 29:3 has only a Study Context record (ot-ezekiel-v29-3).

new.title: Ezekiel is told to proclaim the Lord's day against Egypt
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; 30:1–19 has only a Study Context record at 30:15.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to address Pharaoh and his multitude
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; chapter 31 has no record.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to lament over Pharaoh, king of Egypt
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 32:4 has only a Study Context record (ot-ezekiel-v32-4).

new.title: Ezekiel is told to lament Egypt's descent into the pit
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; the second lament (32:17–32) has only a Study Context record at 32:21.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against Mount Seir

new.title: Jesus tells the disciples to let his betrayal prediction sink in
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Jesus tells the disciples to take in what he is about to say concerning his being handed over.

new.title: Jesus warns a would-be follower about the cost of following him
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Jesus responds to an offer to follow him by describing the Son of Man’s lack of a place to rest.

verified_additional_scripture.context_note: Related passage verified in the contextual review.

new.title: Woe to the towns that saw Jesus' mighty works without repenting
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum (spoken to the seventy-two)
new.note: Jesus contrasts the towns’ response to his works with the repentance Tyre and Sidon would have shown.

verified_additional_scripture.context_note: Related passage verified in the contextual review.

new.title: Jesus gives the seventy-two authority over snakes, scorpions and the enemy
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Jesus describes the authority he has given the seventy-two after they return from their mission.

new.title: Blessed are the eyes that see what the disciples see
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Jesus privately blesses the disciples’ eyes and contrasts what they see with what prophets and kings longed to see.

verified_additional_scripture.context_note: Related passage verified in the contextual review.

new.title: God knows hearts; what people exalt is abomination before Him
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Jesus addresses Pharisees who justify themselves publicly and contrasts human esteem with God’s judgment.

new.title: Heed Moses and the Prophets before it is too late
new.speaker: Jesus (Abraham speaking in the parable)
new.note: Rich man and Lazarus parable has no record; 16:29 'let them hear them' is its directive.

new.title: Jesus teaches how the kingdom of God comes
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the Pharisees asking when the kingdom comes
new.note: Jesus rejects the idea that people can point to the kingdom’s arrival. The Saints Translation renders his answer “within you.”

new.title: Jesus tells Zacchaeus to hurry down because he must stay with him
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Zacchaeus episode has no record; his pledge of fourfold restitution (19:8) belongs in it.

new.title: Pharisees demand that Jesus rebuke his disciples' praise
new.speaker: some Pharisees in the crowd
new.note: 19:37–38 is praise, out of scope; the Pharisees' demand (19:39) and Jesus' refusal could be recorded.

new.title: The Emmaus disciples urge the stranger to stay with them
new.speaker: Cleopas and his companion
new.note: Ordinary hospitality request, comparable to recorded Old Testament hospitality requests.

new.title: The risen Jesus tells the disciples to see and touch him
new.speaker: the risen Jesus
new.recipient: the Eleven and those with them
new.note: Includes his request for food (24:41); same evening as John 20:19–20. Compare AUD-47-20-24 (Thomas).

new.title: Jerusalem's leaders send priests and Levites to question John
new.speaker: the Jews of Jerusalem, from the Pharisees
new.recipient: priests and Levites sent to John
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The inquiry is a particular assignment reported by the narrator. John’s scriptural self-description in verse 23 belongs to the response.

new.title: Jesus invites John's two disciples to come and see
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: Andrew and another disciple of John
new.note: Jesus invites Andrew and the other disciple to see where he is staying.

new.title: Philip invites Nathanael to come and see Jesus
new.speaker: Philip
new.note: A disciple's invitation, echoing Jesus' 'come and see' (1:39).

new.title: Mary tells the servants to do whatever Jesus tells them
new.speaker: Mary, the mother of Jesus
new.recipient: the servants at the wedding in Cana
new.note: Distinct speaker from Jesus' own instructions in AUD-47-2-7 (2:7–8).

new.title: Jesus asks the Samaritan woman for a drink
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: a Samaritan woman at Jacob's well
new.note: An ordinary request of the kind the catalogue records; it crosses the Jewish–Samaritan divide.

new.title: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman to call her husband
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Jesus gives the woman a particular direction during their conversation at the well.

new.title: The Samaritan woman invites her townspeople to come and see Jesus
new.speaker: the Samaritan woman
new.note: Her testimony leads many Samaritans to believe (4:39–42).

new.title: Jesus tells the royal official to go, for his son lives
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: a royal official whose son lay ill in Capernaum
new.note: Healing word like AUD-46-7-11; 4:47 and 4:49 are petitions to Jesus, out of scope.

new.title: Jesus tells the crowd to stop grumbling among themselves
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Includes the Prophets quotation 'they shall all be taught by God' (6:45).

new.title: Jesus' brothers urge him to go to Judea and show himself
new.speaker: Jesus' brothers
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: His brothers urge him to display his works publicly. Jesus’ response and direction to them follow in verses 6–8.

new.title: The chief priests and Pharisees send officers to seize Jesus
new.speaker: the chief priests and Pharisees
new.note: Verse 32 reports the order. In verses 45–49 the officers return without Jesus and explain why.

new.title: Jesus compares himself to the door of the sheepfold
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Jesus uses a figure of speech and explains that salvation comes through him.

new.title: Jesus tells the disciples they will return to Judea for Lazarus
new.speaker: Jesus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Direction to go back despite the threat of stoning; 11:9–10 is reported separately.

new.title: Thomas urges the other disciples to go with Jesus despite the danger
new.speaker: Thomas called Didymus
new.note: A disciple's exhortation to follow Jesus into danger.

new.title: Martha tells Mary that the Teacher is here and calls her
new.speaker: Jesus, his summons relayed by Martha
new.note: Martha conveys the summons to her sister, who goes out to meet Jesus.

new.title: Greek worshipers ask Philip to arrange a meeting with Jesus
new.speaker: some Greeks who came up to worship at the feast
new.note: Ordinary request, passed through Andrew to Jesus; it occasions AUD-47-12-23 (12:23–26).

new.title: Jesus tells Judas to do quickly what he is about to do
new.speaker: Jesus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 13:29: the disciples assumed an errand, buying for the feast or giving to the poor.

new.title: Jesus tells the disciples to rise and leave with him
new.speaker: Jesus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Spoken as he goes to do 'just as the Father commanded Me'.

new.title: Remember that the world hated Jesus before it hated you
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Compare AUD-47-16-1 (remember the warning) and Matthew 10:24–25; the slave-and-master saying recalls 13:16.

new.title: Jesus tells the high priest to question those who heard him
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Appeal to proper testimony, comparable to AUD-47-7-50; 18:23 asks for testimony about any wrong spoken.

new.title: The chief priests ask Pilate to reword the inscription on the cross
new.speaker: the chief priests
new.note: Pilate refuses: 'What I have written, I have written.'

new.title: The soldiers agree to cast lots for Jesus' seamless tunic
new.speaker: the soldiers at the cross
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The soldiers agree among themselves to cast lots for the tunic. The evangelist identifies fulfillment of Greek Psalm 21:19.

new.title: The Jews ask Pilate to break the legs and remove the bodies
new.speaker: the Jewish authorities
new.note: The request concerns removing the bodies before the Sabbath. The soldiers break the legs of the other two men but find Jesus already dead.

new.title: Mary asks the supposed gardener where he has laid Jesus
new.speaker: Mary Magdalene
new.recipient: the risen Jesus, taken for the gardener
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Ordinary request; the commission that follows is AUD-47-20-16.

new.title: The risen Jesus directs the catch and invites the disciples to breakfast
new.speaker: the risen Jesus
new.recipient: seven disciples fishing on the Sea of Tiberias
new.note: Jesus tells the disciples where to cast the net, asks them to bring fish, and invites them to eat.

new.title: Peter rebukes Ananias and Sapphira for lying to God
new.speaker: Peter
new.note: Peter says the property and its proceeds were theirs to control. His rebuke concerns deception about the amount given.

new.title: The Ethiopian official asks about baptism and orders the chariot stopped
new.speaker: the Ethiopian eunuch
new.recipient: Philip and those with the chariot
new.note: The Ethiopian’s question concerns baptism. Luke then reports the order to stop and Philip’s baptism of him.

new.title: Peter says God shows no partiality
new.speaker: Peter
new.note: Peter says God accepts those in every nation who fear him and practice righteousness.

new.title: Peter tells the believers to inform James of his release
new.speaker: Peter
new.recipient: the believers gathered at Mary's house
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 'Report these things to James and the brothers', given after the angel's rescue (AUD-48-12-6).

new.title: Herod orders the guards led away for execution
new.speaker: Herod (Agrippa)
new.note: Reported hostile order, like AUD-44-2-16 (Herod and the boys of Bethlehem).

new.title: Tyre and Sidon win over Blastus and ask Herod for peace
new.speaker: the people of Tyre and Sidon
new.note: The people seek peace with Herod because their country depends on his territory for food.

new.title: Synagogue rulers invite Paul and Barnabas to speak a word of encouragement
new.speaker: the synagogue rulers at Pisidian Antioch
new.note: Shows synagogue order: reading of the law and prophets, then exhortation; Paul answers 'listen' (13:16).

new.title: Paul warns the synagogue against ignoring God’s work
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Paul announces forgiveness and justification through Jesus, then warns his hearers in verse 40 with a prophetic quotation.

new.title: Paul tells the man lame from birth to stand upright
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: a man lame from birth at Lystra
new.note: Healing order like AUD-48-3-4 and AUD-48-9-32; it prompts the Lystra episode (AUD-48-14-11).

new.title: Paul and Barnabas appoint elders in the churches they revisit
new.speaker: Paul and Barnabas
new.recipient: elders of the churches of Lystra, Iconium and Antioch
new.note: The appointment applies to the churches on this return journey. Paul and Barnabas pray with fasting and entrust them to the Lord.

new.title: Peter warns the council against burdening Gentile disciples
new.speaker: Peter
new.recipient: the apostles and elders in council
new.topic: Major Teachings: The Word of Christ Handed On
new.note: Peter calls imposing the yoke a test of God and appeals to salvation through the Lord Jesus’ grace.

new.title: Paul proposes to Barnabas revisiting the churches they planted
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Leads to the dispute over John Mark and the separation of Paul and Barnabas.

new.title: Lydia urges Paul's company to stay at her house
new.speaker: Lydia of Thyatira
new.note: Hospitality request after her household's baptism.

new.title: The Philippian magistrates order Paul and Silas beaten and jailed
new.speaker: the magistrates of Philippi
new.note: Reported orders (16:22–23) after the charge of unlawful customs (16:20–21); the jailer obeys (16:24).

new.title: Thessalonian brothers send Paul and Silas away by night to Berea
new.speaker: the brothers at Thessalonica
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The brothers send Paul and Silas to Berea by night after the unrest in Thessalonica.

new.title: Paul sends word for Silas and Timothy to join him quickly
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: Silas and Timothy, via the escorts returning from Athens
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Paul’s escort receives the order to have Silas and Timothy come quickly. The brothers’ direction to Paul in verse 14 is separate.

new.title: Athenian philosophers ask Paul to explain his new teaching
new.speaker: Epicurean and Stoic philosophers at Athens
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The hearers ask Paul to explain his teaching at the Areopagus.

new.title: Ephesian Jews ask Paul to stay; he promises to return, God willing
new.speaker: the Jews of the synagogue at Ephesus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The people in the Ephesian synagogue ask Paul to stay longer. He declines and says he hopes to return.

new.title: Ephesian believers write asking the Achaian disciples to welcome Apollos
new.speaker: the brothers at Ephesus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The brothers write to the disciples in Achaia to ask them to welcome Apollos.

new.title: Paul sends Timothy and Erastus ahead to Macedonia
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Paul sends Timothy and Erastus to Macedonia while he remains for a time in Asia.

new.title: Friendly officials urge Paul not to enter the theater
new.speaker: some of the Asiarchs
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The disciples prevent Paul from entering. The Asiarchs send him a direct warning about entering the theater.

new.title: Paul tells the Troas believers not to be alarmed over Eutychus
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Spoken as Paul embraces the fallen young man, who is restored; compare AUD-48-9-36 (Tabitha, rise).

new.title: Paul summons the Ephesian elders to meet him at Miletus
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: the elders of the church at Ephesus
new.note: Reported summons that occasions the Miletus charge (AUD-48-20-24, A062).

new.title: Jews from Asia call for help against Paul at the temple
new.speaker: Jews from Asia
new.recipient: the men of Israel at the temple
new.note: Their appeal follows their seizure of Paul and accompanies their accusation.

new.title: Tribune orders Paul bound with two chains and taken to the barracks
new.speaker: Claudius Lysias, the tribune
new.note: The tribune orders Paul bound, then orders him taken into the barracks when the uproar prevents an inquiry.

new.title: Paul asks the tribune for permission to address the people
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Request granted at 21:40; Paul then asks the crowd to hear his defense (22:1).

new.title: Paul asks the Jerusalem crowd to hear his defense
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: the crowd at the temple in Jerusalem
new.note: Paul asks the assembled crowd to hear his defense and addresses them in Hebrew.

new.title: The crowd demands that Paul be removed from the earth
new.speaker: the Jerusalem crowd
new.note: The crowd calls for Paul’s death after hearing him say he was sent to the nations.

new.title: The tribune orders the chief priests and council to assemble
new.speaker: the tribune
new.recipient: the chief priests and the whole council
new.note: Convened to learn the accusation; Paul is set before them (23:1–10).

new.title: The high priest Ananias orders Paul struck on the mouth
new.speaker: Ananias the high priest
new.note: Paul protests that the order violates the law (23:3); 23:4–5 is already linked to C0209.

new.title: The tribune orders troops to snatch Paul from the divided council
new.speaker: the tribune

new.title: Conspirators ask the council to summon Paul for an ambush
new.speaker: more than forty Jewish conspirators
new.note: The conspirators report their prior oath, then ask the chief priests and elders to help arrange an ambush.

new.title: Felix orders Paul held in Herod's praetorium until his accusers arrive
new.speaker: Felix the governor

new.title: Tertullus asks Felix to hear his accusation briefly
new.speaker: Tertullus the advocate
new.note: In verse 4 Tertullus asks Felix to hear his side briefly. Verse 8 appeals to what Felix can learn by examination.

new.title: Felix sends Paul away, then summons him often hoping for a bribe
new.speaker: Felix the governor
new.note: Paul's subjects (righteousness, self-control, coming judgment) are reported without quoted directives.

new.title: The chief priests ask Festus to bring Paul to Jerusalem
new.speaker: the chief priests and leading Jews
new.note: A favor requested to set an ambush on the road; Festus declines (25:4).

new.title: Festus tells the Jewish leaders to bring their accusation at Caesarea
new.speaker: Festus
new.recipient: the influential men among the Jews
new.note: Festus answers the request to transfer Paul by directing the leaders to accompany him to Caesarea.

new.title: Agrippa asks to hear Paul and Festus orders Paul brought in
new.speaker: King Agrippa and Festus
new.recipient: Festus and the officers bringing in Paul
new.note: Agrippa asks Festus to hear Paul. Festus gives the subsequent order that Paul be brought into the audience hall.

new.title: Paul asks King Agrippa to hear him patiently
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Agrippa grants leave to speak (26:1).

new.title: Paul proclaims: repent, turn to God, do works worthy of repentance
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: Jews of Damascus, Jerusalem and Judea, and the Gentiles
new.note: Paul's obedience to the vision (AUD-48-26-15); compare AUD-44-3-7 and AUD-48-3-17.

new.title: Paul warns the ship's company against sailing on from Fair Havens
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: the centurion, pilot, shipowner and crew
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Paul advises against proceeding because he foresees loss. He later reminds the company that the advice was disregarded.

new.title: Paul calls the leading Jews of Rome together to hear him
new.speaker: Paul
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Paul summons the Jewish leaders in Rome to explain his imprisonment. They later set a day to hear his case.

new.title: Do not teach others the law while breaking it yourself
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: the one who bears the name Jew and teaches the law
new.note: Paul challenges the person who teaches others while transgressing the law he teaches.

new.title: Do not do evil so that good may come
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Paul rejects the slogan as slander and calls its proponents' condemnation just; compare 6:1–2.

new.title: As far as it depends on you, live at peace with all
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Paul’s exhortation to live at peace with all has the express qualification “as far as it depends on you.” Verse 17’s prohibition of retaliation belongs with A086.

new.title: Gentile believers owe material service to Jerusalem’s saints
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Paul explains the Macedonian and Achaian contribution to poor believers in Jerusalem in terms of their shared spiritual blessings.

new.title: Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Includes 8:2–3: one who thinks he knows does not yet know as he ought; one who loves God is known by Him.

new.title: Paul urged Apollos to visit Corinth, but he declined for now
new.speaker: Paul
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported request; Apollos will come when he has opportunity.

new.title: Open your hearts wide to us and make room for us
new.speaker: Paul
new.topic: Major Teachings: The Word of Christ Handed On
new.note: AUD-51-6-14 (6:14–7:1) interrupts; 7:2 resumes the appeal. 7:4–7 and 7:12–16 are autobiography.

new.title: Macedonian churches beg Paul to share in the ministry to the saints
new.speaker: the churches of Macedonia
new.note: Reported request (8:4); the rest narrates the Macedonians' example that grounds AUD-51-8-6 (8:6–12).

new.title: James, Cephas and John recognize Paul and Barnabas’s mission
new.speaker: James, Cephas and John, recognizing God's entrusting
new.note: The pillars recognize God’s grace and agree on the respective missions. Verse 9 records that agreement. Verse 10 contains a distinct request about the poor.

new.title: Paul boasts in Christ’s cross and values the new creation
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Paul contrasts his own reason for boasting with the outward show sought by the people pressing for circumcision.

new.title: Paul forbids anyone to trouble him further
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: This prohibition concerns troubling Paul and his situation, even though he addresses a church audience.

new.title: Paul urges steadiness in faith and the hope of the gospel
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Conditional exhortation (1:23); 1:23b 'of which I, Paul, became a servant' leads into AUD-55-1-24.

new.title: All who want to live godly lives in Christ will be persecuted
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Timothy followed Paul's conduct and sufferings (3:10–11); leads into AUD-59-3-14 (3:14–17).

new.title: Paul asks Timothy to come quickly, bringing Mark, his cloak and books
new.speaker: Paul
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Paul asks Timothy to come, bring Mark and retrieve the cloak and books. Verse 21 repeats the urgency before winter.

new.title: Paul tells Titus to come to Nicopolis when Artemas or Tychicus arrives
new.speaker: Paul
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Also reports the planned sending of Artemas or Tychicus to relieve Titus.

new.title: Paul asks Philemon to prepare a guest room for him
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Distinct request (lodging) from the Onesimus appeal; Paul hopes to be released through their prayers.

new.title: The author asks for prayer so he may be restored sooner
new.speaker: the author of Hebrews
new.note: No record after 13:17; compare Paul's prayer requests AUD-57-3-1 and AUD-49-15-30.

new.title: Bear with the word of encouragement
new.speaker: the author of Hebrews
new.topic: Major Teachings: The Word of Christ Handed On
new.note: Closing request to receive the letter's exhortation patiently.

new.title: Do not be surprised if the world hates you
new.speaker: the writer of 1 John
new.note: Direct prohibition between A094 (3:11–12) and A014 (3:15); cf. John 15:18–19 and 1 Peter 4:12 (A054).

new.title: Obedience accompanies confidence before God and abiding in him
new.speaker: the writer of 1 John
new.note: The passage links confidence, prayer and abiding with obedience. Verse 23 states the command itself and is already in A012.

new.title: The trumpet-like voice summons John to come up and see
new.speaker: the first voice John heard, sounding like a trumpet
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: The voice summons John into the heavenly vision. Revelation 1 introduces the trumpet-like voice.

new.title: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord
new.speaker: a voice from heaven, confirmed by the Spirit
new.recipient: John and the hearers of the prophecy
new.note: The blessing itself is separate from the order to write it, which is already recorded as AUD-70-14-13.

new.title: A bowl angel summons John to see the great prostitute's judgment
new.speaker: one of the seven angels with the bowls
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: The angel’s summons shows John a particular judgment. The similar summons in 21:9 introduces a different sight.

new.title: Blessed are those called to the Lamb's marriage supper
new.speaker: the angel speaking with John
new.recipient: John and the hearers of the prophecy
new.note: The angel gives the blessing as the content of a separate order to write, already recorded as AUD-70-19-9.

new.title: Blessed and holy is the one who shares in the first resurrection
new.speaker: John, the narrative voice of the revelation
new.note: Revelation's fifth beatitude has no record; origin follows the narrator's sayings AUD-70-13-9 and AUD-70-13-18. 20:4 'judgment was given' is narrative.

new.title: A bowl angel summons John to see the bride, the Lamb's wife
new.speaker: one of the seven angels with the bowls
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: The angel summons John to see the bride, distinct from the judgment shown in 17:1.

new.restored_from: Claude's recall review U1545, independently verified against Saints Exodus 1:8–12
new.title: Pharaoh appoints labor overseers to afflict the Israelites
new.speaker: Pharaoh, the new king of Egypt
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.review_note: The appointment carries out Pharaoh’s scheme in Exodus 1:10. The overseers receive the assignment, and the Israelites are subjected to the forced labor.

extend.title: Abraham asks his servant to take an oath
extend.note: Abraham's oath forbids a Canaanite marriage, directs his servant to Abraham’s kin, and includes an exception if the woman will not come.

extend.title: Pharaoh sends Abram away with Sarai
extend.note: 12:20: Pharaoh commanded men to escort Abram away with his wife and all he had.

extend.title: Abraham asks to buy Ephron’s cave
extend.note: The request begins in 23:8: 'hear me, and speak for me to Ephron'.

extend.title: Rebekah tells Jacob to bring two young goats
extend.note: 27:10 completes the order: take the food to your father so that he blesses you.

extend.title: Rebekah tells Jacob to stay with Laban until Esau calms
extend.note: The order opens in 27:43 ('arise and flee... to Laban') and ends in 27:45; 27:44 alone is a fragment.

extend.title: Jacob proposes taking marked animals as wages
extend.note: The proposal opens in 30:31 ('You shall give me nothing') and sets the theft test in 30:33.

extend.title: Jacob prepares his servant for Esau’s questions
extend.note: In this numbering the prescribed answer is 32:18–19; the record's 32:17 holds only the marching order.

extend.title: Jacob tells his servants to announce that he is following
extend.note: The announcement itself ('your servant Jacob comes behind us') is 32:21 in this numbering.

extend.title: Jacob presses Esau to accept his gift
extend.note: 33:10 already makes the request: 'receive the gifts from my hands.'

extend.title: Joseph advises Pharaoh to appoint overseers and store grain
extend.note: 41:36 completes the advice: keep the food for the land against the seven years of famine.

extend.title: Joseph orders one brother to fetch the youngest
extend.note: The test is announced in 42:15: you shall not leave unless your youngest brother comes.

extend.title: Joseph tells his detained brothers how to stay alive
extend.note: 42:19 states the terms of 'Do this': one brother held, the rest carry grain home.

extend.title: Judah asks Jacob to send Benjamin with him
extend.note: 43:9 adds Judah's surety: 'require him from my hand'; 43:10 closes the plea.

extend.title: Joseph sends his brothers to bring Jacob to Egypt
extend.note: The message continues: live in Goshen near me, and I will nourish you (45:10–11).

extend.title: Pharaoh assigns Goshen and offers work tending his livestock
extend.note: 47:6 continues: 'settle your father and your brothers in the best of the land'.

extend.title: Jacob asks Joseph to bury him outside Egypt
extend.note: 47:30 completes the request: carry me out of Egypt and bury me in my fathers' tomb.

extend.title: Jacob explains how Joseph’s later children will inherit
extend.note: 48:5 is the main ruling (Ephraim and Manasseh are mine, as Reuben and Simeon); retitle the record accordingly.

extend.title: The workers are told to find straw without a lower quota
extend.note: The proclamation begins in 5:10: 'Thus says Pharaoh: I will no longer give you straw.'

extend.title: Exclude uncircumcised and otherwise ineligible persons from the Passover meal
extend.note: Rambam N126 (12:45) is not itemized; C0111's 'otherwise ineligible persons' covers it. Extend 12:43 to 12:43–45.

extend.title: Accept the keeper's exonerating oath without demanding restitution
extend.note: 22:9 states the case whose ruling C0196 (22:10) records; extend to 22:9–10.

extend.title: Aaron and sons: remain at the tent entrance through the seven days of consecration
extend.note: 8:35 restates and completes C0459 (8:33), adding 'so that you do not die'; extend to 8:33–35.

extend.title: Present a suspected or changing skin lesion to the priest
extend.note: C0484's title covers new and changing lesions; its reference (13:2) omits the repeated directions at 13:9, 16 and 19.

extend.title: Isolate suspected skin or scalp lesions for the specified examination periods
extend.note: C0486's title already covers the boil, burn and scalp cases; its reference stops at 13:4–5.

extend.title: Wash garments after clearance of the specified skin or scalp lesion
extend.note: C0487's title names scalp lesions; 13:34 is the scalp-case washing, outside its 13:6 reference.

extend.title: Burn the garment or leather article with the persistent or recurring lesion
extend.note: C0498's title already covers the unchanged-after-washing and recurring cases stated at 13:55 and 13:57.

extend.title: Wash the affected garment or leather as prescribed, including the second cleansing wash
extend.note: C0499's title names the second cleansing wash, which is stated at 13:58, not 13:54.

extend.title: Present the prescribed eighth-day purification offerings and oil, with the poverty substitutions
extend.note: C0511's title names the poverty substitutions, but these are stated only at 14:21–23.

extend.title: Priest: inspect and classify the house lesion by the stated criteria
extend.note: Rambam P103 (leprous house) is itemized across C0519–C0532; extend C0521 to the re-inspections at 14:44 and 14:48. / Declaring the replastered house clean is part of C0521's classification; extend its reference.

extend.title: Wash garments after the specified contact with a discharge or contaminated bedding
extend.note: Carrying his bedding (15:10) and being touched by unwashed hands (15:11) are further specified contacts; extend C0534–C0536 to 15:5–11.

extend.title: Bathe after the specified contact with a discharge or contaminated bedding
extend.note: Bathe after the specified discharge contact

extend.title: Remain unclean until evening after the specified discharge contact
extend.note: Remain unclean until evening after the specified discharge contact

extend.title: Bathe after the stated seminal emission or intercourse
extend.note: C0543's title names intercourse, stated only at 15:18; its reference stops at 15:16.

extend.title: Observe uncleanness until evening after the stated seminal emission or intercourse
extend.note: C0544's title names intercourse, stated only at 15:18; its reference stops at 15:16.

extend.title: Provide the prescribed personal and congregational animals for the Day of Atonement
extend.note: C0548's title names the congregational animals, which are specified only at 16:5.

extend.title: Do not defile yourselves through the prohibited sexual acts
extend.note: Extend C0594 (18:24) to 18:24–30; 18:26 binds natives and resident foreigners alike. / 18:29 states the penalty (cut off); 18:30 repeats the charge not to be defiled.

extend.title: Priests: do not approach or eat holy things while unclean
extend.note: Rambam N75 (unclean priest not to serve) is itemized as C0670 (22:3–7); 22:2 is its heading. / 22:9 is the closing sanction for 22:1–8; it could instead attach to C0672.

extend.title: Do not profane Israel's holy contributions
extend.note: 22:16 completes the sentence begun at 22:15.

extend.title: Proclaim God's appointed feasts at their prescribed times
extend.note: 23:4 repeats C0679's charge (23:2) as the heading of the festival calendar.

extend.title: Set apart the prescribed tithe of produce and livestock as holy to God
extend.note: Rambam P78 (cattle tithe) is named in C0759's title, but its reference stops at 27:30; extend to 27:30–32.

extend.title: Israel: march in the prescribed tribal and tabernacle order
extend.note: The order of setting out continues beyond 2:9; extend C0773 to 2:9–31.

extend.title: Take the Levites and their livestock in place of Israel's firstborn
extend.note: 3:45 repeats C0781 (3:41) after the count; extend to 3:41–45.

extend.title: Register the three Levite divisions within the stated service ages
extend.note: C0784's title names all three divisions, but its reference covers only the Kohathites (4:2–3); add 4:22–23 and 4:29–30. / Merarite census; see the C0784 note at 4:22–23.

extend.title: Use the prescribed trumpet calls to assemble the people or leaders
extend.note: 10:7 specifies C0844's assembly call (10:3–4).

extend.title: Bring the prescribed congregational bull and goat for the stated inadvertent failure
extend.note: 15:22–23 state the case that C0859 (15:24–26) answers.

extend.title: Do not assign Aaron's and Levi's tribe an ordinary territorial inheritance
extend.note: C0881's title names Levi's tribe; 18:23–24 restate it for the Levites.

extend.title: Observe seven-day uncleanness after the specified human corpse, bone, grave or death-house contact
extend.note: C0895's title already covers death-house, bone and grave contact but cites only 19:11. Rambam P107 is itemized at C0895.

extend.title: Balak asks Balaam to curse Israel
extend.note: 22:5 sends the envoys and opens the message that 22:6 completes.

extend.title: Balak offers Balaam a reward for cursing Israel
extend.note: Opening plea of the same message whose reward offer (22:17) is recorded.

extend.title: Apply the stated confirmation or timely annulment rules to a wife's vow
extend.note: A wife's vow in her husband's house, including late annulment (30:16); C0932 cites only 30:7–9. 30:17 is a closing summary.

extend.title: An inheriting daughter: marry within the father's clan under the tribal-land provision
extend.note: Generalizes the ruling for Zelophehad's daughters (36:6) to every inheriting daughter.

extend.title: Preserve ancestral tribal allotments against transfer to another tribe
extend.note: Restates 36:7.

extend.title: The eastern tribes must cross armed ahead of Israel
extend.note: Completes the 3:18–19 order.

extend.title: Joshua and Israel: do not fear the coming kingdoms
extend.note: Opening of the same charge to Joshua whose 'do not fear' (3:22) is recorded.

extend.title: Do not destroy food-producing trees for siegeworks
extend.note: Extend C1100 from 20:19 to 20:19–20: the permitted exception completes the tree law.

extend.title: Keep the military camp from evil and indecency
extend.note: C1149's title ('indecency') already draws on 23:15; extend its reference from 23:10 to 23:10, 15.

extend.title: Recite the prescribed ancestral-deliverance declaration when presenting firstfruits
extend.note: Rambam P132 is itemized as C1198, but its reference (26:3) omits the recited declaration itself (26:5–10).

extend.title: Set up and plaster the prescribed covenant stones on Mount Ebal
extend.note: C1203's title already names Mount Ebal, which only 27:4 supplies; extend from 27:2 to 27:2, 4.

extend.title: Write the law clearly on the covenant stones
extend.note: C1204's 'clearly' comes from 27:8 ('very plainly'); extend from 27:3 to 27:3, 8.

extend.title: Choose the life God sets before you
extend.note: The two-ways appeal (30:15–20) is one unit; extend C1212 from 30:19.

extend.title: Joshua tells Israel what to say about the Jordan memorial
extend.note: 4:6 holds the children's question that the answer in 4:7 replies to.

extend.title: Joshua tells Israel how to explain the dry crossing to their children
extend.note: The instruction runs from the children's question (4:21) through the words and purpose (4:23–24).

extend.title: Joshua orders the troops to rise from ambush and take Ai
extend.note: 8:5–6 (the feigned flight) are the first half of the order completed in 8:7–8.

extend.title: Israel’s leaders decide to spare Gibeon because of their oath
extend.note: 9:19 states the prohibition itself: 'now we cannot touch them.'

extend.title: The Lord tells Joshua to divide the remaining land among the tribes
extend.note: 'Only distribute it by lot' (13:6) begins the same allotment command.

extend.title: Joshua tells Ephraim and Manasseh to clear the woodland allotment
extend.note: Joshua first gives the woodland instruction at 17:15; 17:17–18 repeats and expands it.

extend.title: The Lord has Gideon dismiss the fearful and test the rest
extend.note: Outside candidate list. 7:5 gives the test itself (set apart those who lap like dogs). Candidate 7:13 is narrative.

extend.title: Samson states the stakes of his wedding riddle
extend.note: Outside candidate list. 14:12 states Samson’s side of the wager; the recorded 14:13 states theirs.

extend.title: The host offers two women to the mob instead of his guest
extend.note: 19:23 (‘please do not act wickedly… do not commit this folly’) opens the plea that 19:24 completes.

extend.title: Ruth asks Naomi to let her stay and pledges loyalty
extend.note: 1:17 completes Ruth’s pledge (‘where you die, I will die’) with her self-curse oath.

extend.title: The priests prescribe gold mice and tell the Philistines to honor the Lord
extend.note: 6:4 prescribes the five gold seats that the 6:5 record omits; 6:6 warns against hardening hearts like Pharaoh.

extend.title: Israel asks Samuel for a king to judge them
extend.note: 8:5 holds the elders’ actual request (‘Now appoint a king over us’); 8:6 only restates it.

extend.title: Saul orders slaughter at the stone so Israel will not eat blood
extend.note: Outside candidate list. 14:33 ‘Roll a large stone here to me’ begins the order. Candidates 14:28–29 fall under P00700.

extend.title: Samuel teaches Saul that obedience is better than sacrifice
extend.note: Outside candidate list. 15:23 completes the saying: divination is sin, and rejecting the Lord’s word costs the kingship.

extend.title: Goliath challenges Israel to send a champion
extend.note: 17:9 sets the terms of the challenge: the loser’s people serve the winner’s.

extend.title: David asks Jonathan to let him hide during the new moon feast
extend.note: 20:6 gives the excuse Jonathan is to tell Saul (delivered at 20:28–29); 20:7 sets the test of Saul’s reaction.

extend.title: Jonathan asks David to show lasting kindness to his family
extend.note: The request begins at 20:14 (‘you shall show mercy to me’) and closes with Jonathan’s renewed oath (20:16–17).

extend.title: Jonathan explains which arrow signal means it is safe
extend.note: Outside candidate list. 20:22 gives the danger signal: ‘the shaft is beyond you… go’.

extend.title: Jonathan’s call to the boy signals David to hurry away
extend.note: 20:36 ‘Run, find the shafts’ and 20:37 ‘the shaft is beyond you’ belong to the same signal sequence.

extend.title: David forbids Abishai from striking Saul
extend.note: Adds 26:10–11: David restates the prohibition and orders, ‘take the spear… and the water flask, and let us go.’

extend.title: Saul asks the medium at Endor to summon Samuel
extend.note: Adds 28:8, Saul’s first request (‘divine for me… bring up the one I name’), with his oath of safety in 28:10.

extend.title: Tamar resists Amnon and pleads with him to stop
extend.note: Adds 13:13, where her plea continues: ‘Please speak to the king now, for he certainly will not withhold me from you.’

extend.title: David asks Hushai to send reports through the priests’ sons
extend.note: Adds 15:35 (‘Whatever you hear from the king’s house, tell Zadok and Abiathar’), between the 15:34 and 15:36 records.

extend.title: Absalom summons Hushai for a second opinion
extend.note: Adds 17:6, the request itself (‘Should we act on his proposal? If not, you speak’); Hushai’s answer is first-pass P00793.

extend.title: David asks Judah’s elders to bring him back
extend.note: Adds 19:13, the rest of the message: ‘You are my brothers… Why should you be the last to bring the king back?’

extend.title: The wise woman of Abel calls for Joab to speak with her
extend.note: Adds 20:17: ‘Hear your handmaid’s words.’

extend.title: Nathan advises Bathsheba to remind David of his oath about Solomon
extend.note: Adds 1:14, the last step of Nathan’s plan: he will come in after her and complete her words.

extend.title: David charges Solomon to keep the Lord’s commands in Moses’ law
extend.note: Adds 2:4, completing the sentence with God’s conditional promise: ‘If your sons guard their way, walking before Me in truth.’ 2:5 needs nothing.

extend.title: David tells Solomon to hold Shimei to account
extend.note: Adds 2:8, which names Shimei, his curse and David’s oath; the Greek doublet is 1 Kings 2:35l–35o.

extend.title: The Lord tells Elijah to hide at the Chorrath wadi
extend.note: Adds 17:4, the rest of the instruction: drink from the wadi; the ravens will feed him there.

extend.title: Jezebel’s letters order a fast and seat Naboth before the people
extend.note: The letter continues in 20:10: suborn two false witnesses and stone Naboth; the title should name this.

extend.title: The Syrian advisers propose replacing the kings with governors
extend.note: The counsel runs 21:23-25: fight on level ground and rebuild the lost army horse for horse.

extend.title: Elisha tells the young prophet to take Jehu aside privately
extend.note: The instruction begins in 9:1: fasten your belt, take the flask of oil, go to Ramoth-gilead.

extend.title: Jehu tells his officer to throw Joram’s body into Naboth’s field
extend.note: The order is completed in 9:26: 'lift him up and throw him into the portion, according to the Lord's word.'

extend.title: Jehu summons Baal’s worshipers under false pretenses
extend.note: The summons is sent throughout Israel with its threat in 10:21.

extend.title: Joash directs the priests to use the silver to repair the temple
extend.note: Outside candidate list: the order begins in 12:5 by naming the silver to be received.

extend.title: Joash answers Amaziah with the story of the thornbush and cedar
extend.note: The fable's application follows in 14:10: enjoy your glory at home; why court disaster?

extend.title: Hezekiah asks Isaiah to pray for the remnant
extend.note: Hezekiah's message to Isaiah begins in 19:3.

extend.title: Josiah sends his scribe to the high priest to account for the silver
extend.note: Adds 22:3: the date and ‘the king sent Sapphan… saying’, which introduces the commission.

extend.title: Josiah asks his officials to seek the Lord about the recovered book
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 22:12 introduces the order ('The king commanded...').

extend.title: David proposes bringing the ark back among the people
extend.note: The proposal begins in 13:2: send for the brethren, priests and Levites to gather.

extend.title: Joab urges courage in defending their people and cities
extend.note: The mutual-rescue arrangement (19:12) opens the same charge.

extend.title: David calls Israel’s leaders to seek the Lord and build the sanctuary
extend.note: 22:17 reports the command to support Solomon that the speech (22:18-19) delivers.

extend.title: Jahaziel tells Judah to go out and watch the Lord deliver them
extend.note: 'Tomorrow go down against them', with the enemy’s position; same oracle and directive. Extend to 20:16–17.

extend.title: Jehoiada assigns priests and Levites to Sabbath gate duty
extend.note: Completes the assignment by thirds begun in 23:4 (cf. 2 Kings 11:5–6 records); extend to 23:4–5.

extend.title: Josiah sends his officials to seek the Lord about the recovered book
extend.note: 34:20 names the officials commanded; cf. first-pass P00951 (2 Kings 22:12–13).

extend.title: Huldah tells the officials to take the Lord’s answer back to Josiah
extend.note: Second 'this is what you shall say to him' charge in the same oracle; extend to 34:23–26 (cf. 2 Kings 22:18).

extend.title: The king’s officers press Mattathias to obey the decree first
extend.note: 2:17 opens the same appeal, flattering Mattathias’s standing.

extend.title: The fugitives resolve to defend themselves on the Sabbath
extend.note: The deliberation that produces the 2:41 resolution; extend to 2:40–41.

extend.title: Mattathias urges his sons to rally those who keep the law and avenge their people
extend.note: Same deathbed charge continues ('Repay the nations… attend to the law’s command'); extend to 2:67–68.

extend.title: Judas proposes fighting while his men urge retreat
extend.note: Judas’s reply, 'let us die courageously for our brothers', completes the exchange; extend to 9:8–10.

extend.title: Demetrius asks for continued loyalty and promises rewards
extend.note: The promised remissions and gifts are the reward named in the record’s title; extend to 10:27–28.

extend.title: Apollonius challenges Jonathan to learn who supports him
extend.note: Challenge 'come down to us into the plain' (10:71); extend to 10:70–73 and retype Study Context as Command (cf. ot-2-kings-v14-8).

extend.title: Simon charges his sons to lead the nation in battle
extend.note: 16:2 names the sons summoned and opens the charge.

extend.title: A mother urges her youngest son to trust God and face death without fear
extend.note: Opening of the same appeal ('Son, have mercy on me…'); extend to 7:27–29.

extend.title: Cyrus calls for volunteers to rebuild God’s house in Jerusalem
extend.note: 1:1 is the order to proclaim it in writing; the record already links 2 Chronicles 36:22–23, which includes it.

extend.title: The king orders the rebuilding of Jerusalem to stop
extend.note: Adds 4:22, the same decree’s charge: be on guard against slackness lest harm increase to kings.

extend.title: Cyrus directs that the temple vessels be returned
extend.note: 5:14 names Sasabasar, who receives the vessels and the order.

extend.title: Darius orders officials to leave the temple work alone and fund it
extend.note: Adds 6:6, the opening of the same order (‘keeping far away from there’).

extend.title: Ezra charges the priests to guard the sacred gifts until Jerusalem
extend.note: Adds 8:24–28: Ezra sets apart the twelve, weighs the offerings into their hands and declares them and the vessels holy.

extend.title: Ezra recalls the ban on intermarriage with the peoples of the land
extend.note: The quoted commandment begins in 9:11.

extend.title: Ezra calls the assembly to separate from foreign wives
extend.note: 10:10 opens Ezra’s charge with the indictment.

extend.title: The proposal calls for officials to bring young women to Susa
extend.note: Adds 2:4, the same proposal’s last clause: the woman who pleases the king shall reign in Astin’s place.

extend.title: Mordecai warns Esther that the palace will not spare her
extend.note: Outside candidate list (4:14): the warning continues, 'Who knows whether you became queen for this time?'

extend.title: Esther asks the Jews of Susa to fast before she approaches the king
extend.note: 4:15 introduces Esther’s message to Mordecai.

extend.title: Heed your father's discipline and your mother's teaching
extend.note: v9 gives the promised reward: a crown of graces and a golden collar.

extend.title: Do not let wrongdoers lead you astray
extend.note: vv11–14 quote the sinners' enticement to bloodshed and a common purse.

extend.title: Keep away from the path of wrongdoers
extend.note: vv16–18 give the reasons: they run to evil and store up evils for themselves.

extend.title: Seek wisdom like treasure to learn justice and reverence
extend.note: vv10–11 complete the conditional promise: wisdom in the heart and good counsel will guard you.

extend.title: Do not be taken in by counsel that forgets God's covenant
extend.note: vv16, 18–19: evil counsel's house lies beside death; none who go return.

extend.title: Take your teacher's instruction to heart
extend.note: v2 gives the motive: length of life, years of living and peace.

extend.title: Fear God and turn from evil instead of relying on your own wisdom
extend.note: v8 promises healing for the body and care for the bones.

extend.title: Honor the Lord with the firstfruits of honest work
extend.note: v10 promises full storerooms and vats gushing with wine.

extend.title: Hold fast to wise counsel
extend.note: The following verses continue the same counsel with its promised safety, healing, and peace.

extend.title: Do not delay help or plot against a neighbor
extend.note: v32 gives the reason for v31: every lawless person is unclean before the Lord.

extend.title: Keep the teaching handed down from your father
extend.note: v3: the teacher recalls being taught as an obedient son, introducing his father's words.

extend.title: Honor wisdom and she will lift you up
extend.note: v9 promises a crown of graces and of delight.

extend.title: Receive wise teaching for a long life
extend.note: vv11–12: he teaches straight tracks where steps are not hampered.

extend.title: Hold on to discipline and avoid the ways of the wicked
extend.note: vv16–17 give the reason: the wicked cannot sleep unless they do harm.

extend.title: Keep wise words in your heart
extend.note: v22: they are life to those who find them and healing for all flesh.

extend.title: Listen to wisdom before the warning about seduction
extend.note: v2 completes the charge: 'I command you to heed the discernment of my lips.'

extend.title: A warning about the seductive power of flattering speech
extend.note: vv4–6: her sweetness turns bitter; her feet lead down to death and Hades.

extend.title: Keep away from the seducer's house
extend.note: vv9–10: lest your life and your labors go to strangers.

extend.title: Act quickly to free yourself from a pledge
extend.note: vv1–2 state the case: surety for a friend snares you by your own lips.

extend.title: Bind your parents' teaching close to your heart
extend.note: v22: take it along when you walk; let it guard your sleep.

extend.title: Do not let desire for beauty ensnare you
extend.note: v26 gives the reason: such a woman hunts men's precious lives.

extend.title: Guard wise teaching as you guard your eyes
extend.note: v5: so that wisdom keeps you from the alien woman's pleasing words.

extend.title: Do not let your heart turn toward adultery
extend.note: Verses 26–27 finish the warning, and 7:6–23 is the narrative illustration leading into the warning. It is context for the counsel.

extend.title: Wisdom invites the inexperienced to learn discernment
extend.note: vv1–4: Wisdom stands at the gates and summons all humankind.

extend.title: Wisdom calls her listeners to hear what is right
extend.note: vv7–9: her words are truth and righteousness, plain to the discerning.

extend.title: Value discipline and discernment above silver and gold
extend.note: v11: wisdom is better than costly stones.

extend.title: Wisdom invites the foolish to her table
extend.note: vv1–4: Wisdom builds her house, prepares her feast and sends servants to call the foolish.

extend.title: Keep away from Folly's invitation
extend.note: v18b states what fleeing her place means: crossing the foreign water.

extend.title: The warning against drinking from a foreign spring
extend.note: v18d gives the reward: long life and added years.

extend.title: Listen to the wise and take their words to heart
extend.note: Extend 22:17 to 22:17–21: keep, recite and copy the sayings so your hope rests in the Lord.

extend.title: Do not mistreat the poor or shame the weak in court
extend.note: Adds the motive clause: the Lord will judge their case.

extend.title: Choose companions who are not quick to anger
