extend.note: Adds the motive clause: lest you learn his ways and ensnare yourself.

extend.title: Do not make a pledge just to please someone
extend.note: Adds the motive clause: your bedding will be taken if you cannot pay.

extend.title: Do not strain to keep up with the rich
extend.note: Adds the motive: riches vanish, flying off on eagle's wings.

extend.title: Beware of dining with a begrudging host
extend.note: Adds the motive: he eats and drinks as one who swallowed a hair.

extend.title: Respect old boundaries and the property of orphans
extend.note: Adds the motive: the orphans' mighty Redeemer will judge their case.

extend.title: Seek understanding and attend to a child's discipline
extend.note: 23:14 completes the sentence: the rod rescues the child's life from death.

extend.title: Fear the Lord instead of envying sinners
extend.note: Adds the promise: you will have offspring and your hope will not depart.

extend.title: A warning against excess in drink and food
extend.note: Adds the motive: drunkards and the sleepy come to poverty and rags.

extend.title: Give your parents reason to rejoice
extend.note: 23:24 states the same point: a righteous father rejoices over a wise son.

extend.title: Avoid drunkenness and seek righteous company
extend.note: Extend 23:31 to the whole poem on wine's woes, 23:29–35.

extend.title: Do not envy evil people or seek their company
extend.note: Adds the motive: their hearts plot lies and their lips speak trouble.

extend.title: A warning about the wicked near the righteous
extend.note: Adds the motive: the righteous fall seven times and rise again.

extend.title: Do not rejoice when an enemy falls
extend.note: Adds the motive: the Lord will see, be displeased and turn His wrath away.

extend.title: Do not celebrate evildoers or envy sinners
extend.note: Adds the motive: the wicked have no future and their lamp goes out.

extend.title: Honor God and the king
extend.note: Verse 22 gives the reason for this counsel; 22a–22e are separate sayings.

extend.title: Speak truthfully to a king
extend.note: Greek plus: the king's sword-like tongue and consuming wrath give the reason for truthful speech.

extend.title: Wait to be invited forward and do not rush into a dispute
extend.note: 25:10 completes 25:9: lest your friend reproach you and enmity remain. Unlettered 25:10 only.

extend.title: Do not trust an enemy's pleading voice
extend.note: Adds the deceitful enemy's agreeable lips (26:24) and the exposure of hidden enmity (26:26).

extend.title: Know your flocks and give attention to your herds
extend.note: Extend 27:23 to the unit 27:23–27: strength does not last, so tend pasture and flocks.

extend.title: Do not add to God's words
extend.note: Adds the ground: every word of God is refined, and He shields those who revere Him.

extend.title: Wine for those in grief or pain
extend.note: Adds the purpose: so they forget their poverty and troubles.

extend.title: Praise the capable woman’s reverence and honor her work
extend.note: 31:28–29 give the children's and husband's praise that 31:30–31 commends.

extend.title: Cling to God and endure changing circumstances
extend.note: 2:5 is the reason clause of 2:4.

extend.title: Remember how God answered those who trusted him
extend.note: 2:11 grounds 2:10: the Lord is compassionate, forgives sins and saves.

extend.title: A father's call to listen and put his teaching into practice
extend.note: 3:2 gives the reason for 3:1 and opens the section on honoring parents.

extend.title: Honor your father in both word and deed
extend.note: 3:9 is the reason clause of 3:8.

extend.title: Do not take pride in a parent's disgrace
extend.note: 3:11 is the reason clause of 3:10.

extend.title: Support your father patiently in old age
extend.note: 3:14–15 give the reason: kindness to a father is credited against sins.

extend.title: Act gently and stay humble as your standing grows
extend.note: 3:20 is the reason clause of 3:18; 3:19 is absent from this text.

extend.title: Do not neglect people who are poor or hungry
extend.note: 4:6 is the reason clause of 4:5.

extend.title: Recognize the right moment and guard against evil
extend.note: 4:21 explains 4:20's call not to be ashamed: one shame brings sin, another glory.

extend.title: Do not defer to others at your own expense
extend.note: 4:24 is the reason clause of 4:23: wisdom is known through speech.

extend.title: Do not let pride tear you apart
extend.note: 6:3–4 complete the warning of 6:2: an evil soul destroys its owner.

extend.title: Wisdom grows through a willingness to learn
extend.note: 6:33 is the parallel line to 6:32.

extend.title: Do not show off in times of trouble
extend.note: 10:27 is the better-than saying grounding 10:26; cf. Proverbs 12:9.

extend.title: Honor yourself with gentleness
extend.note: 10:29 is the reason clause of 10:28.

extend.title: Do not judge another person by appearance
extend.note: 11:1 (the humble person's wisdom exalts him) and 11:3 (the small bee's sweet product) frame 11:2.

extend.title: Do not boast in clothes or status
extend.note: 11:5–6 illustrate 11:4: rulers brought low, the unsuspected crowned.

extend.title: Trust God and keep working without envying wrongdoers
extend.note: 11:22 completes the reason given in 11:21.

extend.title: Do not assume present ease will last
extend.note: 11:25 grounds 11:23–24: good days forget the bad, and bad days the good.

extend.title: A person's happiness cannot be judged before death
extend.note: 11:26–27 lead into 11:28: at death the Lord repays and a person's works are revealed.

extend.title: Be discerning about whom you welcome into your home
extend.note: 11:30–32 elaborate 11:29's warning about the ambushes of the deceitful.

extend.title: Sirach distinguishes support for the humble from support for wrongdoing
extend.note: 12:6 is the reason clause of 12:4–5.

extend.title: Remain watchful when an enemy pretends to be humble
extend.note: 12:10 begins the copper-and-mirror image that 12:11 completes.

extend.title: Be alert around those who can bring you down
extend.note: 13:12 is the reason for the watchfulness of 13:13; 13:14 is absent from this text.

extend.title: Remember death and do good for a friend while you can
extend.note: 14:15 is the reason for 14:14 and 14:16: your toil will be divided among heirs.

extend.title: Pursue wisdom as a tracker follows a trail
extend.note: 14:23–24 continue the image of 14:22: peering through her windows, pitching a tent by her walls.

extend.title: Do not blame God for going astray
extend.note: 15:13 continues the reasons of 15:11–12.

extend.title: The teacher values godly children over a large family
extend.note: 16:4 is the reason clause of 16:3: one person of understanding settles a city.

extend.title: Listen and take knowledge to heart
extend.note: 16:25 completes the call of 16:24; 16:26–30 are a creation hymn, out of scope.

extend.title: God's charge to avoid injustice toward one's neighbor
extend.note: 17:11–13 recount the giving of the law and covenant that frames the charge in 17:14.

extend.title: Return to God and turn away from sin
extend.note: 17:24 introduces the call of 17:25.

extend.title: Return to the Most High and reject injustice
extend.note: 17:27–29 give the reasons: the dead cannot praise, and His mercy to those who return is great.

extend.title: Do not spoil a kindness with reproach
extend.note: 18:16–18 develop 18:15: a word is better than a gift, and a fool's gift wounds.

extend.title: Do not repeat what was said in confidence
extend.note: Verse 9 completes the warning about repeating what another said.

extend.title: Let an unneeded report end with you
extend.note: 19:11–12 contrast the fool who labors to release a word.

extend.title: Flee sin as you would a snake
extend.note: 21:3 continues the images of 21:2: lawlessness is a two-edged sword.

extend.title: Mourning for the dead and for the loss of understanding
extend.note: 22:12 completes 22:11: mourning for the dead lasts seven days, for a fool all his life.

extend.title: Avoid needless argument with a fool
extend.note: 22:14–15 give the reason for 22:13.

extend.title: Learn to control your speech
extend.note: 23:8 is the reason clause of 23:7; the prayer in 23:1–6 is out of scope.

extend.title: Do not make a habit of swearing oaths
extend.note: 23:10–11 give the reasons: habitual swearing fills a house with lawlessness and calamity.

extend.title: A warning against deadly speech among God's people
extend.note: 23:15 closes the unit: one accustomed to abusive words is never instructed.

extend.title: Wisdom invites those who desire her to share her fruit
extend.note: 24:17 names the fruit offered in 24:19; 24:20–21 give the reasons. 24:18 is absent.

extend.title: Sirach's advice to fathers about watching over daughters
extend.note: 26:12 completes the warning of 26:11; extend 26:10–11 to 26:10–12.

extend.title: Listen to a person speak before praising their judgment
extend.note: 27:4–6 (sieve, furnace, fruit images) ground 27:7; extend 27:7 to 27:4–7.

extend.title: Be faithful to a friend and guard their secrets
extend.note: 27:16 states the principle (revealing secrets destroys trust); extend 27:17 to 27:16–17.

extend.title: The image of a friendship lost through betrayal
extend.note: 27:18–19 and 27:21 complete the images around 27:20; extend 27:20 to 27:18–21.

extend.title: Lend to a neighbor in need and repay debts on time
extend.note: 29:1 (mercy lends) and 29:3 (keep faith with the lender) frame 29:2; extend to 29:1–3.

extend.title: The image of giving to the poor as stored treasure
extend.note: 29:13 continues the image (almsgiving fights for you); extend 29:12 to 29:12–13.

extend.title: Remember the favor of someone who guaranteed your debt
extend.note: 29:14, 16 contrast the good guarantor with the ungrateful debtor; extend 29:15 to 29:14–16.

extend.title: Be content with little or much while a guest
extend.note: 29:21–22, 24 give the reasons (own roof better; a guest's life is grievous); extend 29:23 to 29:21–24.

extend.title: Do not surrender to grief and brooding
extend.note: 30:22 is the reason (gladness of heart is life); extend 30:21 to 30:21–22.

extend.title: Take comfort and do not let grief consume you
extend.note: 30:24–25 continue the reason (jealousy and anxiety shorten days); extend 30:23 to 30:23–25.

extend.title: Eat with restraint and know when to stop
extend.note: 31:19–20 give the reasons (a little suffices; moderation brings healthy sleep); extend 31:16–18 to 31:16–20.

extend.title: Do not try to prove your strength through drinking
extend.note: 31:26 is the reason (wine tests hearts in quarrels); extend 31:25 to 31:25–26.

extend.title: Consider the contrasts among God's works
extend.note: 33:14 states the pairs (good/evil, life/death, sinner/godly) that 33:15 tells the reader to consider.

extend.title: The teacher asks leaders to hear counsel on household affairs
extend.note: 33:22 is the reason for 33:19–21 (better your children ask of you); extend 33:18–21 to 33:18–22.

extend.title: Sirach's ancient household advice on forced labor and punishment
extend.note: 33:25 opens the same counsel (fodder, rod and work); extend 33:26–29 to 33:25–29.

extend.title: Do not put your trust in dreams without grounds
extend.note: 34:5, 7–8 surround 34:6 (omens are vain; dreams mislead; the law proves true); extend 34:6 to 34:5–8.

extend.title: The teacher calls worshipers to bring an offering
extend.note: 35:5–6 give the reason (the righteous one's offering is accepted and remembered); extend 35:4 to 35:4–6.

extend.title: Give generously and offer firstfruits with gladness
extend.note: 35:10 is the reason (the Lord repays sevenfold); extend 35:7–9 to 35:7–10.

extend.title: Consider whose interests an adviser is serving
extend.note: 37:7 (some counsel for themselves) and 37:9 (end of 37:8's sentence) belong to it; extend 37:8 to 37:7–9.

extend.title: Recognize what harms you and refrain from it
extend.note: 37:28 is the reason (not everything benefits everyone); extend 37:27 to 37:27–28.

extend.title: Exercise restraint with food and luxury
extend.note: 37:30–31 give the reasons (illness; many die of insatiability); extend 37:29 to 37:29–31.

extend.title: Honor the physician and recognize the need for care
extend.note: 38:2–3 give the reasons (healing is from the Most High; the physician's honored skill); extend 38:1 to 38:1–3.

extend.title: Mourn the dead and see to their burial
extend.note: 38:18–19 give the reason for limiting mourning (grief brings death); extend 38:16–17 to 38:16–19.

extend.title: Sirach's severe warning about a life of begging
extend.note: 40:29–30 give the reasons (dependence defiles; begging burns within); extend 40:28 to 40:28–30.

extend.title: Remember others who have died and do not fear death
extend.note: 41:4 is the reason (death is the Lord's sentence on all flesh); extend 41:3 to 41:3–4.

extend.title: Guard a good name more than great wealth
extend.note: 41:11, 13 frame 41:12 (sinners' names are blotted out; a good name endures); extend 41:12 to 41:11–13.

extend.title: Sirach's advice to fathers about a daughter's reputation
extend.note: 42:9–10 (a father's sleepless anxieties) lead into 42:11; extend 42:11–12 to 42:9–12 (see P01862).

extend.title: Look at the rainbow and bless its maker
extend.note: 43:12 completes the rainbow sentence (the Most High stretched it out); extend 43:11 to 43:11–12.

extend.title: God's greatness surpasses all the praise we can give
extend.note: 43:27–28 lead into 43:29–30 (we never reach the end; He is greater); with P01864 combined extension is 43:27–33.

extend.title: Job's wife urges him to speak to God and die
extend.note: Her speech begins at 2:9 ('How long will you persist…?'); extend the reference to the whole speech, 2:9–9e.

extend.title: Bildad urges Job to seek God in prayer
extend.note: Adds 8:6, the condition joined to the call: ‘If you are pure and true, He will hear your supplication.’

extend.title: Bildad urges Job to consult earlier generations
extend.note: Adds 8:9–10: the reason (we are of yesterday) and the promise that the fathers will teach him.

extend.title: Zophar challenges Job’s speech and his claim to innocence
extend.note: Adds 11:4: ‘Do not say, I am pure in my works and blameless before Him.’
extend.updated_title: Zophar challenges Job’s speech and his claim to innocence

extend.title: Job asks his friends to stop shaming him
extend.note: Adds 19:2–4 and 19:6: ‘How long will you weary my soul?… Know, then, that the Lord is the One who disturbed me.’

extend.title: Job appeals to what travelers have seen
extend.note: The sentence runs on: the travellers' signs show the wicked are kept for the day of destruction.

extend.title: Eliphaz urges Job to take God's words to heart
extend.note: Adds 22:21 (‘become firm… your fruit will be among good things’) and 22:23 (‘turn back and humble yourself before the Lord’).

extend.title: Elihu asks to be heard and questions whether age guarantees wisdom
extend.note: Adds 32:11–13: ‘Give ear to my words’, and his warning that they not say they have found wisdom.

extend.title: Elihu calls for attention to his argument
extend.note: Adds 34:17: ‘Look at the One who hates lawless things and destroys the wicked.’

extend.title: Elihu asks Job to look at the distant clouds
extend.note: Adds 35:6–8: your sin or righteousness affects only humans like you, not God.

extend.title: God calls Job to prepare for questioning
extend.note: Adds 38:4 ‘Report to Me, if you understand’; later ‘tell Me’ challenges are Study Context (38:18), hence low.

extend.title: God tells Job's friends to bring offerings and seek his prayer
extend.note: The Lord's speech to Eliphaz begins at 42:7 with its reason: you did not speak truly, as Job did.

extend.title: The warning against being as unthinking as a mule
extend.note: Extend from 31:9 to 31:8–9: 'I will instruct you in the way you will go' introduces the same counsel.

extend.title: Taste God's kindness and put your hope in him
extend.note: Outside candidate list: extend from 33:9–10 to 33:8–11: the angel encamping (33:8) and 'seekers lack no good thing' (33:11) frame it.

extend.title: Turn from evil and do good
extend.note: Extend from 36:27 to 36:27–29: 'For the Lord loves judgment… the righteous will dwell for ever' completes '…and dwell for age upon age'.

extend.title: A call to watch the path of the upright and peaceful
extend.note: Extend from 36:37 to 36:37–40: the contrast (lawless destroyed) and 'salvation of the righteous is from the Lord' complete it.

extend.title: The royal song calls the king to reign for truth and justice
extend.note: Extend from 44:5 to 44:4–5: 'Gird your sword… and stretch forth, prosper and reign' is one sentence.

extend.title: Do not be afraid when others grow rich
extend.note: Extend from 48:17 to 48:17–21: the 'for when he dies he takes nothing' reasons and refrain complete the counsel.

extend.title: A warning to those who forget God
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 49:23 ('a sacrifice of praise will glorify Me') concludes God's speech and is uncovered; cf. 49:14.

extend.title: A song calling all the earth to praise God
extend.note: Extend from 65:1–2 to 65:1–4: 'Say to God, How fearsome are Thy works…' continues the same call to all the earth.

extend.title: A warning against defiance and unjust speech
extend.note: Outside candidate list: extend from 74:6 to 74:6–9: 'for God is judge; He humbles one and raises another' grounds the warning.

extend.title: A call to sound instruments and the new moon trumpet
extend.note: 80:5–6 ground the trumpet call: 'an ordinance for Israel… a testimony in Joseph' (cf. Numbers 10:10, C0848).

extend.title: Love the Lord and hate evil
extend.note: v11 gives the motive: light has dawned for the righteous, gladness for the upright.

extend.title: A call for the whole earth to make music to God
extend.note: v6 continues the imperatives: shout before the King with trumpets and horn.

extend.title: The Lord calls the addressee to sit at His right hand and rule among enemies
extend.note: The oracle continues in 109:2 with a second imperative: 'Exercise dominion in the midst of your enemies.'
extend.updated_title: The Lord calls the addressee to sit at His right hand and rule among enemies

extend.title: The person who reveres the Lord is compassionate, lends and gives
extend.note: v10 completes the portrait: the sinner rages and his desire perishes.

extend.title: A call for the Lord's servants to praise his name
extend.note: v3 repeats the imperative: praise the Lord's name from sunrise to sunset.

extend.title: Do not place your trust in mortal rulers
extend.note: 145:4 gives the reason and 145:5 the contrasting beatitude: happy is the one whose helper is the God of Jacob.

extend.title: Speak carefully and sparingly before God
extend.note: Adds the motive: a fool's voice comes with many words.

extend.title: Recognize the limits and risks of accumulating wealth
extend.note: 5:15–16 conclude the unit: one departs as one came, having toiled for wind.

extend.title: A warning against excessive righteousness and wisdom
extend.note: 7:15 is the observation the warning answers: the righteous perish while the wicked endure.

extend.title: Do not take every word people say to heart
extend.note: Adds the motive: you yourself have often cursed others.

extend.title: Wisdom for dealing with a king and an oath
extend.note: 8:4–5 complete the counsel: the king's word has authority; whoever keeps the command avoids harm.

extend.title: Remember your Creator while you are young
extend.note: 12:2–7 are the 'before…' clauses of the same command, picturing old age and death.

extend.title: The conclusion calls for reverence and obedience to God
extend.note: Adds the ground: God will bring every deed into judgment.

extend.title: A call for judges to love justice and seek God
extend.note: 1:2–5 give the grounds: God is found by those who trust Him; wisdom shuns deceit.

extend.title: A warning against grumbling and slander
extend.note: 1:6–10 ground the 'therefore' of 1:11: God's Spirit fills the world and hears every word.

extend.title: A warning against bringing ruin on oneself
extend.note: 1:13–16 ground the warning: God did not make death; the ungodly summon it.

extend.title: Rulers are called to learn wisdom and answer for their conduct
extend.note: 6:10 gives the motive: those who keep holy things in holiness will be made holy.

extend.title: Giving thanks to God at daybreak
extend.note: 16:29 is the reason clause of 16:28's maxim; 16:27 gives the manna image it draws on.

extend.title: The Lord calls for justice for the wronged, the orphan and the widow
extend.note: 1:19–20 complete the 1:18 invitation (obey and eat the land's good; refuse and the sword devours); extend 1:17–18 to 1:17–20.

extend.title: Isaiah’s hearers are told to regard the Lord as holy
extend.note: 8:14–15 give the attached promise and warning (sanctuary or stumbling stone); extend 8:13 to 8:13–15. Quoted Romans 9:33; 1 Peter 2:8.

extend.title: The Lord gives Eliakim the robe and authority of the steward
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 22:20 (I will call Eliakim) and 22:22–23 (David’s glory, established ruler) complete the appointment.

extend.title: Isaiah warns the wealthy women about failed crops
extend.note: 32:9 ('rise and hear my voice') opens the address recorded at 32:10–12.

extend.title: Hezekiah’s delegation asks Isaiah to pray for the survivors
extend.note: Hezekiah sends the delegation (37:2) and its message begins at 37:3; first pass likewise extended 2 Kings 19:4 to 19:3–4.

extend.title: The servant is to call prisoners into freedom and light
extend.note: 49:8 ('I gave you as a covenant for nations… saying to those in bonds') begins the sentence recorded at 49:9.

extend.title: The people who seek the Lord are called to remember their origins
extend.note: 51:2 completes the same directive ('Look at Abraham your father and Sarah').

extend.title: The Lord calls people away from what cannot satisfy
extend.note: 55:1 opens the invitation continued in 55:2; echoed in Revelation 22:17 (AUD-70-22-17) and John 7:37 (AUD-47-7-37).

extend.title: God tells young Jeremiah to go where he is sent and speak His words
extend.note: 1:5 is the appointment ('I have appointed you a prophet to nations'); 1:6 is the objection answered in 1:7.

extend.title: God tells Jeremiah to rise and speak without fear
extend.note: 1:18–19 complete the charge: a fortified city and bronze wall against Judah’s kings, rulers and people.

extend.title: Jeremiah is told to speak the covenant words to Judah
extend.note: 11:3 continues the charge ('you will say to them') with the curse on whoever will not hear; bridges records 11:2 and 11:4.

extend.title: The oracle calls for Babylon’s storehouses to be opened and destroyed
extend.note: 27:27 continues the same summons: 'Dry up all her fruits, and let them go down to slaughter.'

extend.title: Moab’s neighbors are called to mourn the breaking of its power
extend.note: 31:20 continues the same summons: 'Wail and cry out; announce at Arnon that Moab perished.'

extend.title: The survivors ask Jeremiah to seek the Lord’s direction
extend.note: The request begins in 49:2: 'Pray to the Lord your God for these survivors.'

extend.title: Ezekiel is sent to speak the Lord’s words to the exiles
extend.note: 3:10–11 is one charge: 'take into your heart all the words… and go, enter the captivity.'

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to depict Jerusalem under siege
extend.note: 4:1 begins the same sign: take a brick and draw the city Jerusalem on it.

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to lie on his side as a sign of Israel’s guilt
extend.note: 4:6 completes the sign: lie on the right side forty days for Judah, a day for a year.

extend.title: Ezekiel announces judgment to the mountains and valleys of Israel
extend.note: 6:2 holds the charge itself: ‘set your face firmly against the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them’.

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to enter and see the people’s wrongdoing
extend.note: ‘Son of man, dig’ (8:8) opens the way for ‘Go in and see’; one continuous order.

extend.title: Judgment in the vision begins at the sanctuary and spares the marked
extend.note: 9:7 completes the order: defile the house, fill the roads with the dead, go out and strike. Long record AUD-30-9-3 omits it.

extend.title: Ezekiel covers his face and goes out as a sign
extend.note: 12:3–5 hold the rest of the exile sign (ready baggage by day, dig through the wall); 12:7 reports his compliance.

extend.title: Ezekiel charges Jerusalem with bloodshed and idolatry
extend.note: 22:2 holds the charge itself: 'display all her lawless deeds to her, and say'.

extend.title: The oracle summons a crowd against Oholah and Oholibah
extend.note: 23:47 continues the same imperatives: stone them and pierce them.

extend.title: Ezekiel addresses Tyre as a proud center of maritime trade
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 27:2 holds the charge 'take up a lament over Tyre'.

extend.title: Ezekiel addresses Israel’s land after neighboring peoples dishonor it
extend.note: 36:1 opens the same charge: 'prophesy concerning Israel's mountains and say'.

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to speak the Lord’s word over the dry bones
extend.note: 37:5–6 is the word he must speak; 37:7 records that he prophesied as commanded.

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to call the breath from the four winds
extend.note: 37:10 records his obedience: 'I prophesied as He commanded me'.

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to write Judah and Joseph on two staffs
extend.note: 37:17 'join them as one staff' completes the sign; 37:18–20 tells him how to explain it.

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to deliver the Lord’s warning to Gog
extend.note: 38:2 holds the charge: 'set your face against Gog… and prophesy against him'.

extend.title: A grain and oil offering accompanies the morning sacrifice
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 46:13 prescribes the daily morning lamb itself, now only in broad record ot-ezekiel-v46-1.

extend.title: The decree to execute Babylon’s wise men
extend.note: 2:12 is the king's order itself; 2:14 names Arioch as the one ordered to carry it out.

extend.title: The accusers cite the king’s decree to worship the image
extend.note: 3:11 is the decree's penalty clause (the blazing furnace).

extend.title: Darius orders his kingdom to worship Daniel’s God
extend.note: 6:28 completes the decree with Darius's own pledge and its reason.

extend.title: Gabriel tells Daniel why he came to explain the vision
extend.note: 9:22 opens the same explanation: 'I have just come out to show you understanding.'

extend.title: Hosea calls Israel to return to the Lord with a confession
extend.note: 14:4 continues the words Israel is told to take: Assyria will not save us; no more horses or handmade 'gods'.

extend.title: The Lord calls the people to consider their ways
extend.note: 1:7 repeats the 1:5 call (‘Place your hearts upon your ways’) before the rebuilding order in 1:8.

extend.title: The Lord sends Zerubbabel a message about shaking heaven and earth
extend.note: The message runs to 2:23, where the Lord chooses Zerubbabel and makes him like a signet.

extend.title: The Lord calls the dispersed to flee the northern land
extend.note: 2:11 continues the same call (‘Escape safely to Zion’); AUD-42-2-7’s note already treats 2:10–11 as one unit.

extend.title: The Lord questions whom the people fasted for
extend.note: 7:6 completes the same question: their eating and drinking, like their fasting, was for themselves.

extend.title: The Lord warns the priests to honor His name
extend.note: 2:1 introduces the same charge: 'And now this command is for you, priests.'

extend.title: Malachi warns against abandoning the wife of one’s youth
extend.note: The charge begins at 2:13–14: offerings are refused because they abandoned the wife of their youth.

extend.title: The Lord calls the people to return after straying from His ordinances
extend.note: The sentence ‘you, sons of Jacob, do not refrain from the injustices of your fathers’ begins in 3:6.

extend.title: The Lord challenges the people to test His provision through the dues
extend.note: 3:8–9 name what is withheld, the tithes and firstfruits ('you are defrauding Me'), which the 3:10 challenge concerns.

extend.review_note: The Lord’s message to Ahaz ends with a conditional warning connecting belief to understanding.
The oracle specifies the shepherds’ self-enrichment and their neglect of the weak, the sick, the injured, and the lost.

extend.title: Jesus calls fishermen to follow him
extend.note: Not a listed candidate: the call of James and John (4:21–22) is uncovered. Mark 1:16–20 is also unlinked.

extend.title: Let your light shine so others glorify the Father
extend.note: 5:14–15 (light of the world, lamp on the stand) lead directly into the command of 5:16.

extend.title: Reconcile with your brother and settle with your accuser
extend.note: 5:26 completes the settlement warning; the linked Luke 12:57–59 already includes its parallel (12:59).

extend.title: Ask, seek, and knock
extend.note: 7:9–11 (the Father gives good things to those who ask) parallel Luke 11:11–13, already linked.

extend.title: Beware of false prophets and recognize them by their fruit
extend.note: Not a listed candidate: 7:17–20 (good and rotten trees) are uncovered and complete the same teaching.

extend.title: Jesus tells his critics to learn why God desires mercy
extend.note: Not a listed candidate: 9:12 (the physician saying) opens the same reply; Mark 2:17 and Luke 5:31–32 are also unrecorded.

extend.title: Jesus sends the Twelve to Israel to proclaim the kingdom and heal freely
extend.note: 10:1’s grant of authority parallels Luke 9:1–2, already linked; Mark 6:7 is also unlinked.

extend.title: Trust what will be given to say when you are handed over
extend.note: 10:17–18 open the same warning; its Mark 13:9 parallel ('they will hand you over to councils') is already linked.

extend.title: Jesus tells his disciples whom to fear
extend.note: 10:29–31 (sparrows, numbered hairs, 'So do not fear') are already linked in their Luke 12:6–7 form.

extend.title: Jesus says it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath
extend.note: 'Stretch out your hand' (12:13) completes the scene; the linked Luke 6:6–11 already includes the same healing order.

extend.title: Jesus warns against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees
extend.note: 16:11–12 repeat the warning of 16:6 and explain it as the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

extend.title: Deny yourself, take up your cross, and follow Jesus
extend.note: Outside candidate list; 16:26–27 (gaining the world, forfeiting life; repaid by conduct) complete the call, as the linked Luke 9:24–26.

extend.title: Jesus calls his disciples to turn and become like children
extend.note: Outside candidate list; the question of greatness (18:1–2) and 'whoever receives one such child receives Me' (18:5) frame 18:3–4.

extend.title: Jesus teaches on marriage and Moses’ permission to divorce
extend.note: The testing question opens the teaching; first pass widened the Mark link to 10:2–12 the same way (B20 P02640).

extend.title: Jesus tells the rich man to keep the commandments
extend.note: The question 'what good thing shall I do?' (19:16) is the occasion of the command in 19:17.

extend.title: Seek greatness through serving others
extend.note: The contrast with the rulers of the nations (20:25) opens the teaching; the ten's indignation (20:24) is its occasion.

extend.title: Give Caesar what is Caesar’s and God what is God’s
extend.note: The tribute question and 'Show Me the coin' (22:17–19) lead directly into the command of 22:21.

extend.title: Jesus warns his disciples against claiming religious titles
extend.note: Outside candidate list; 23:11–12 close the unit (servant greatness, the self-exalted humbled), as K054 and Luke 14:11 (K056).

extend.title: Jesus rebukes neglect of justice, mercy, and faithfulness
extend.note: Outside candidate list; 'straining out the gnat but swallowing the camel' (23:24) completes the tithing woe.

extend.title: Stay watchful because the time is unknown
extend.note: The ten virgins parable (25:1–12) is the illustration whose application, 25:13, the record already holds.

extend.title: Jesus identifies with the least of his brothers
extend.note: The judgment scene (25:31–39) leads to 25:40; 25:41–46 is already linked. Covers candidates 25:37–39 (P02582).

extend.title: Jesus tells the disciples to watch and pray in Gethsemane
extend.note: Adds the setting, the charge to watch, and Jesus’ return to the disciples. Verse 39 is Jesus’ prayer to the Father.

extend.title: Make disciples of all nations, baptize them, and teach them
extend.note: The eleven go to the mountain 'where Jesus had directed them' (28:16; compare 28:10 in AUD-44-28-5), setting the commission.

extend.title: Jesus declares the Son of Man Lord of the Sabbath
extend.note: The Pharisees' charge, 'not lawful on the Sabbath' (2:24), is the occasion; the linked Luke 6:1–5 already includes it.

extend.title: Attend to what you hear
extend.note: Outside candidate list; the lamp on the stand (4:21–22) opens the same unit. Luke 8:16–18 (candidate 8:18) parallels 4:21–25.

extend.title: Jesus tells his disciples not to stop someone acting in his name
extend.note: John’s report in verse 38 supplies the occasion for Jesus’ response. Verse 41 is a separate promise.

extend.title: Have salt in yourselves and live at peace
extend.note: Outside candidate list; 'everyone will be salted with fire' (9:49) leads into the salt saying of 9:50.

extend.title: Love God with heart, soul, mind, and strength
extend.note: The scribe's question 'Which commandment is first of all?' opens it; first pass linked Matthew 22:34–38 likewise (B20 P02573).

extend.title: Jesus silences and expels the unclean spirit
extend.note: The crowd's 'With authority and power He commands the unclean spirits' (4:36) reports the same command.

extend.title: Rise, carry the bed, and go home
extend.note: 'Rise and walk' (5:23) introduces the order of 5:24; he obeys in 5:25.

extend.title: Love your enemies, do good, and lend freely
extend.note: The 'what credit is that to you?' contrasts (6:32–34) lead straight into 6:35.

extend.title: Report what Jesus is doing
extend.note: John sends two disciples with the question that Jesus' charge answers; first pass linked Matthew 11:2–6 the same way (B20 P02528).

extend.title: Recognize the connection between forgiveness and love
extend.note: 7:48–50 complete the scene: 'Your sins are forgiven... Your faith has saved you; go in peace.'

extend.title: Hear and hold the word with perseverance
extend.note: Adds the opening of the parable before the existing call to hear and its explanation.

extend.title: Give the crowd something to eat
extend.note: The Twelve's 'Dismiss the crowd' (9:12) is the request Jesus answers with 'You give them something to eat.'

extend.title: Show mercy as the Samaritan did
extend.note: Record holds only the application (10:36–37); link the parable body, including the care paid for at the inn (10:35).

extend.title: Guard against greed and reliance on possessions
